## Claims
- [source-backed] The supplied primary excerpt defines
  \[
  J_v:=\Bbbk\text{-span}\{\sigma_u:u\ge v\},
  \]
  and calls it an ideal; here the source works with a characteristic-zero field \(\Bbbk\). [source-2, lines 126-139; source-2, lines 328-339]
- [proved] Assume \(A\) has Schur \(\mathbb Z\)-basis \(\{s_\mu:\mu\subseteq q^r\}\), is generated by \(h_1,\ldots,h_q\), and satisfies integral Pieri. Then
  \[
  S=\bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Zs_\mu
  \]
  is an ideal of \(A\).
- [proved] Under the additional Schur-span premise
  \[
  J_v^{\mathbb Z}=\bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Zs_\mu
  \quad\text{inside }A,
  \]
  one has \(J_v^{\mathbb Z}=S\); after scalar extension, \(J_v=\Bbbk\otimes_{\mathbb Z}S\).
- [unsupported] The supplied primary passages do not provide the needed identification between the Bruhat-span definition \(J_v=\Bbbk\text{-span}\{\sigma_u:u\ge v\}\) and the Schur span indexed by \(i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq q^r\). They also do not define an integral \(J_v^{\mathbb Z}\subseteq A\). Thus literal equality \(J_v=S\) is not source-grounded from the supplied material.

## Strategy
For \(i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq q^r\), integral Pieri gives
\[
h_k s_\mu=\sum_{\substack{\nu\supseteq\mu\\ \nu/\mu\text{ horizontal }k\text{-strip}\\\nu\subseteq q^r}}s_\nu.
\]
Every surviving \(\nu\) contains \(\mu\), hence contains \(i^j\); therefore \(h_kS\subseteq S\) for \(1\le k\le q\). Since \(A\) is generated by \(h_1,\ldots,h_q\), this implies \(AS\subseteq S\), proving that \(S\) is an ideal.

The desired equality is then immediate only if the missing Schur-span identification is supplied as a premise.

## Gaps
The required Bruhat-to-Schur correspondence, including its coefficient-ring and quotient-map formulation, is absent from the supplied source excerpts.

## Next
Obtain the primary-source passage establishing the identification of \(J_v\) with the rectangle-containment Schur span; then the conditional equality above becomes unconditional.
